channel.title: Nick Gustafson
channel.description: Writing by Nick Gustafson — software engineer and data scientist. Notes on machine learning, the systems behind it, and the things worth understanding deeply.

item.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search is Awesome
item.description: Monte Carlo Tree Search, from random games to AlphaZero.

item.title: A little experiment in evading AI detection
item.description: Notes from trying to make an AI-drafted series sound human.

item.title: My Throw Decides My Aim
item.description: A D-A-D song leads us to latent space thinking.

item.title: Vectors, Matrices, and the Spaces They Live In
item.description: Vectors as lists of activations, matrix multiplication as a linear map, and how these operations fit into neural networks.

item.title: Norms, Dot Products, and Similarity
item.description: How vector length, dot products, cosine similarity, and projections support attention scores and embedding comparisons.

item.title: Distributions, Softmax, and the Chain Rule of Words

item.description: Why cross-entropy is the standard LM loss, what it actually measures about two distributions, and how it connects to perplexity.

item.title: Gradients and How Machines Learn
item.description: What a gradient is, why it points uphill, how backpropagation computes one efficiently via the chain rule, and what SGD does with it.

item.title: Word2vec and the Embedding Revolution

item.title: GloVe, FastText, and the Embedding Zoo
item.description: How GloVe fits co-occurrence statistics, how FastText shares subword vectors, and where the methods differ.

item.title: Recurrent Neural Networks and Sequence Modeling
